For the sacrifice has Me as its master, since it has been said, "I alone here am the Adhiyajña" (Gītā 8.4). And yet they do not know Me in truth, that is, as I really am. Therefore, having sacrificed not-according-to-rule, they fall away (pra-cyavante) from the fruit of the sacrifice.
BG_C09_V25: Those who vow to the gods go to the gods; those who vow to the ancestors go to the ancestors; those who sacrifice to the bhūtas go to the bhūtas; and those who sacrifice to Me come to Me.
BG_C09_V25::block-0: Even those who, being devotees of other deities, worship not-according-to-rule — for them too the fruit of the sacrifice is inevitable. How? —
BG_C09_V25::block-1: Those whose vow, restraint, and devotion is fixed upon the gods are deva-vratāḥ; they go to, that is, reach, the gods. Those devoted to the manes — the pitṛ-vratāḥ, who are intent on śrāddha and similar rites — go to the manes, namely the agniṣvāttas and the rest. Those who are bhūtejyāḥ, the worshippers of the bhūtas, go to the bhūtas — namely the Vināyaka, the host of the Mātṛs, the Caturbhaginīs, and so on. The mad-yājins — the Vaiṣṇavas, those whose nature it is to sacrifice to Me — go to Me alone. The purport is: though the effort is the same, out of ignorance they do not worship Me; consequently they become partakers of only meagre fruit.
BG_C09_V26: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water — that, devotion-borne, I accept from him whose self is purified.
BG_C09_V26::block-0: Not only is the fruit of My devotees endless, characterised by non-return, but I am also easily worshipped. How? —
BG_C09_V26::block-1: Whoever offers Me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water (toyam = water) — that leaf and the rest, brought near with devotion, that is, presented with devotion as its antecedent, hence "bhakty-upahṛtam" — I accept (aśnāmi = I receive) from one whose self is purified, whose understanding is purified.
BG_C09_V27: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in oblation, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, O son of Kuntī — do that as an offering to Me.
BG_C09_V27::block-1: Whatever you do that has come of itself; whatever you eat; whatever oblation (havana) you accomplish, śrauta or smārta; whatever you give, that is, bestow upon brāhmaṇas and the like — gold, food, ghee and the rest; whatever austerity you undertake, O son of Kuntī — that do as an offering to Me, an act of dedication to Me (mat-samarpaṇam).
BG_C09_V28: Thus you will be released from the bondages of action — those whose fruits are auspicious and inauspicious; with self yoked in the yoga of renunciation, freed, you will come to Me.
BG_C09_V28::block-0: Hear what becomes of you who act thus —
BG_C09_V28::block-1: By such karma-bandhanas — actions whose fruits are auspicious and inauspicious, that is, desirable and undesirable, are called śubhāśubha-phala karmas; the actions themselves are bondages, hence karma-bandhanāni — by these you, while making the offering to Me, will be released. This very thing is called saṁnyāsa-yoga: it is renunciation inasmuch as it is dedication to Me, and it is yoga inasmuch as it is performance of action; therefore by that saṁnyāsa-yoga having become yoked in self — that is, in inner instrument (antaḥkaraṇa) — you, the saṁnyāsa-yoga-yukta-ātmā, freed from the bondages of action even while alive, and when this body falls, will come to Me, that is, attain Me.
BG_C09_V29: I am the same in all beings; none is hateful to Me, none dear. But those who worship Me with devotion are in Me, and I too am in them.
BG_C09_V29::block-0: (Objection:) Then the Lord must be possessed of attachment and aversion, since He favours the devotees but not others. To dispel this —
BG_C09_V29::block-1: I am the same — equal — in all beings; to Me none is an object of hatred, and none an object of love. I am like fire: as fire does not remove the cold of those who stand at a distance, but does remove it from those who draw near, even so do I favour the devotees, not others. But those who worship Me — the Lord — with devotion, in them I dwell — by their very nature, not because of any partiality on My side. And in them, likewise, I too am present by their very nature, not in others. Yet from this it does not follow that I bear any hatred towards the rest.
BG_C09_V30: Even if a man of most evil conduct worships Me with undivided devotion, he is to be regarded as righteous, for he has resolved aright.
BG_C09_V30::block-0: Hear now the greatness of devotion to Me —
BG_C09_V30::block-1: Even if (api cet) — that is, although — one be sudurācāra, exceedingly evil in conduct, of the most despicable behaviour, yet, if he worships Me as ananyabhāk — possessed of undivided devotion, with no other object — he alone is to be regarded as sādhu, of righteous conduct, that is, to be known as such. For he has resolved samyak — rightly, as it ought to be — vyavasita, with firm determination; since his resolve is the resolve of a saint.
BG_C09_V31: Quickly he becomes righteous-minded and attains lasting peace. Know it for certain, O son of Kuntī: My devotee never perishes.
BG_C09_V31::block-0: And, having shed his outward evil conduct through the inner force of his right resolve —
BG_C09_V31::block-1: Quickly, swiftly, he becomes a man of dharma, of righteous mind, and reaches śaśvat — perpetual — peace, that is, abiding tranquillity. Hear now the highest truth: O son of Kuntī, make this firm declaration, take this as a vow — that My devotee, he whose inmost self has been surrendered unto Me, never perishes.
BG_C09_V32: For, O Pārtha, taking refuge in Me, even those born of sinful wombs — women, vaiśyas, and likewise śūdras — they too attain the supreme goal.
BG_C09_V32::block-1: For (hi), O Pārtha, having taken refuge in Me — that is, having grasped Me as their support — even those who may happen to be pāpa-yoni, those whose womb of birth is sinful (the samāsa is vigrahaḥ: pāpā yoniḥ yeṣāṁ te pāpa-yonayaḥ), born of degraded birth. Who are these? He explains: women, vaiśyas, and likewise śūdras — they too travel to the supreme, the highest, goal.
BG_C09_V33: How much more, then, holy brāhmaṇas and devoted royal sages! Having reached this transient and joyless world, worship Me.
BG_C09_V33::block-0: How much more (kim punaḥ), then, the brāhmaṇas, the holy ones, those of meritorious birth — and devotees who are royal sages (rājarṣayaḥ: kings who are also ṛṣis — rājānaḥ ca te ṛṣayaḥ ca rājarṣayaḥ). Since this is so, having attained this anitya — fleeting, perishing in a moment — and asukha — devoid of joy — world, this human world, having gained the rare instrument of human birth which is the means to all the puruṣārthas, worship Me, serve Me.
BG_C09_V34: Be of mind fixed on Me, devoted to Me, sacrificing to Me, bow down to Me. Yoking the self thus, with Me as the supreme refuge, you shall come to Me alone.
BG_C09_V34::block-1: Let your mind be set on Me — Vāsudeva — so be man-manāḥ. Likewise be My devotee, My worshipper — one whose habit is to sacrifice to Me. And bow down to Me alone. To Me alone, the Lord, you shall come — you shall arrive — having yoked, having concentrated, the mind in samādhi. Thus, the self being yoked: I am the Self of all beings, the highest goal, the supreme refuge — and to Me, of such a nature, you shall come (this is the syntactic completion with what was said earlier), being mat-parāyaṇaḥ — having Me as the supreme resort. Such is the meaning.
BG_C10_V01::block-0: In the seventh chapter the true nature (tattva) of the Lord and His manifestations (vibhūtis) were set forth, and likewise in the ninth. Now, however, those particular bhāvas — modes of being — in which the Lord is to be contemplated must be stated; and the tattva of the Lord must also be stated, even though it has been stated already, for it is exceedingly hard to know. Hence the Blessed Lord said —
BG_C10_V01::block-1: Yet again (bhūyaḥ eva — again, once more), O mighty-armed one, hear from Me — that is, mine — the supreme word: paramam, the highest, that which reveals the unsurpassable Reality; the speech which is supreme, addressed to you, who are dear to Me — for, hearing My word, you take exceeding delight, as one drinking nectar; therefore I shall declare it out of my desire for your welfare, with the wish to do you good.
BG_C10_V02: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great ṛṣis know My origin; for I am, in every way, the source of the gods and of the great ṛṣis.
BG_C10_V02::block-0: For what reason will I declare it? — to that He says —
BG_C10_V02::block-1: Neither do they know — that is, do not comprehend — that is, the hosts of devas, Brahmā and the rest. What is it they do not know? My prabhava — taken either as prabhāva, the supreme excellence of My sovereign power, or as prabhava, origination, coming into being. Nor do the great ṛṣis — Bhṛgu and others — know it. Why is it that they do not know? It is now declared: because I Myself am the cause, the origin (ādi), of the gods and of the great ṛṣis, in every manner — in every aspect.
BG_C10_V03: He who knows Me as the unborn, beginningless, and the great Lord of the worlds — he, undeluded among mortals, is freed from all sins.
BG_C10_V03::block-1: He who knows Me as unborn (aja) and beginningless (anādi) — for I am the source of the gods and the great seers, and there exists no other source of Mine; therefore I am unborn and beginningless. The state of beginninglessness is the ground of being unborn: for one who has no prior cause, no birth can be predicated of him. Such a Me, who is unborn and beginningless, whoever knows — that is, comprehends — and knows further as the great Lord of the worlds (loka-mahā-īśvara), the supreme sovereign of all worlds, the Fourth (turīya), wholly free from ignorance and its effects: he, being undeluded (asaṃmūḍha), free from delusion, that man, among mortals, among human beings, is freed from all sins (sarva-pāpaiḥ pramucyate) — from every kind of evil, whether committed knowingly or unknowingly, deliberate or inadvertent: he is utterly released from them all.
BG_C10_V04: Intelligence, knowledge, freedom from delusion, forbearance, truthfulness, control of the senses, control of the mind, pleasure, pain, becoming, non-becoming, fear and also fearlessness —
BG_C10_V04::block-0: And on this further account too I am the great Lord of the worlds —
BG_C10_V04::block-1: Buddhi (intelligence) — the inner organ's capacity for the apprehension of subtle and other objects; it is by reason of possessing this that one is called "intelligent." Jñāna (knowledge) — the cognition of the Self and the other categories. Asaṃmoha (freedom from delusion) — discriminative engagement, preceded by clear discernment, with the matters that present themselves to be understood. Kṣamā (forbearance) — the unaltered state of mind in one who has been reviled or even struck. Satya (truth) — speech is called true when, regarding what has been seen and heard and the experience of one's own self, it is uttered just as it stands, with the purpose of conveying it into the apprehension of another. Dama (control) — the quieting of the outer sense-organs. Śama — the quieting of the inner organ. Sukha (pleasure) — gladness. Duḥkha (pain) — distress. Bhava (becoming) — coming into being. Abhāva (non-becoming) — its opposite. Bhaya (fear) — terror; and abhaya (fearlessness) is its opposite.
BG_C10_V05: Non-injury, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame and infamy — these manifold dispositions of beings arise from Me alone.
BG_C10_V05::block-0: Ahiṃsā (non-injury) — not afflicting living beings. Samatā (equanimity) — even-mindedness. Tuṣṭi (contentment) — satisfaction, the conviction "this much suffices" with respect to gains. Tapas (austerity) — chastening of the body preceded by restraint of the senses. Dāna (giving) — sharing according to one's capacity. Yaśas (fame) — the renown that arises from dharma. Ayaśas (infamy), on the other hand, is the disrepute that arises from adharma. These dispositions (bhāvāḥ) — buddhi and the rest as enumerated above — arise in beings, in living creatures, from Me alone, from the Lord, manifoldly, in many varieties, in accordance with their own respective karma.
BG_C10_V06: The seven great seers of old, and likewise the four Manus, share My nature and were born of My mind; from them sprang these creatures in the world.
BG_C10_V06::block-1: The seven great seers (mahā-ṛṣayaḥ sapta) — Bhṛgu and the rest; "of old" (pūrve) — pertaining to a past age. The four Manus (catvāro manavaḥ), likewise, are those well known as the Sāvarṇas. They are mad-bhāvāḥ — having their disposition centred on Me, endowed with Vaiṣṇava power; mānasāḥ — produced by mind alone; jātāḥ — born, brought forth, by Me. From these Manus and great seers proceeds the creation, in the world, of these creatures bearing the marks of the immobile and the mobile.
BG_C10_V07: Whoever knows in truth this manifestation and this yoga of Mine, becomes joined to unwavering yoga; herein there is no doubt.
BG_C10_V07::block-0: "This" (etām) — the manifestation as just described, the vibhūti, the extension of glory. "And the yoga" — the conjoining, the bringing together pertaining to the Self; or else "yoga" means the power of yogic sovereignty, the omniscience born of yoga: this is what is termed yoga. "Of Mine" — My yoga. Whoever knows this in truth, that is, just as it is, in its very reality — that man becomes joined, becomes united, with unwavering (avikampena), unmoving yoga, characterised by steadiness in right vision (samyag-darśana-sthairya). "Herein there is no doubt" — in this matter no doubt remains.
BG_C10_V08: I am the source of all; from Me everything proceeds. So knowing, the wise, endowed with deep conviction, worship Me.
BG_C10_V08::block-0: What sort of "unwavering yoga" is it that one is joined to? — this is now stated:
BG_C10_V08::block-1: "I" — the supreme Brahman, named Vāsudeva — am the source (prabhava), the origination, of all this universe. From Me alone proceeds the entire universe in its forms of modification — characterised by maintenance, dissolution, action, fruition and enjoyment. "So" — having thus understood — they worship, they serve, Me; namely the wise (budhāḥ), those who have grasped the ultimate reality, the supreme tattva. They are bhāva-samanvitāḥ — bhāva is bhāvanā, the firm settling of the mind upon the supreme reality; endowed (samanvitāḥ) with that, that is, fully joined to it: this is the meaning.
BG_C10_V09: With minds fixed on Me, with their life-breaths gone unto Me, enlightening one another and ever speaking of Me, they remain content and rejoice.
BG_C10_V09::block-1: Mac-cittāḥ — those whose citta, mind, is in Me, are mac-cittāḥ. Mad-gata-prāṇāḥ — those whose prāṇas, the eye and the rest, have gone, that is, attained, to Me, are mad-gata-prāṇāḥ; the meaning is, those who have withdrawn their organs into Me. Or else mad-gata-prāṇāḥ may mean: those whose very life (jīvana) has gone to Me. Bodhayantaḥ — making one another, mutually, comprehend; and speaking together (kathayantaḥ) of Me as distinguished by the qualities of knowledge, strength, valour and the rest. They reach contentment, attain perfect satisfaction, and find delight too — they obtain rati, even as one does in the company of a beloved.
BG_C10_V10: To them, ever steadfast and worshipping Me with affection, I grant that yoga of intellect by which they come unto Me.
BG_C10_V10::block-0: Those who, in the manners just described, worship Me as devotees —
BG_C10_V10::block-1: To them — to those who are ever steadfast (satata-yuktānām), constantly attentive, in whom every outward longing has ceased — to those who worship, who serve. "By reason of what — desire of gain or some such motive?" — No, He says: prīti-pūrvakam, with affection (prīti), with love (sneha), as its motive force; the sense is, to them who worship Me with such love. "I grant" — I bestow — "that buddhi-yoga" (the yoga of intellect): buddhi here is right vision (samyag-darśana) whose sphere is My own reality; the yoga that consists in that is buddhi-yoga; that buddhi-yoga, that is, by which buddhi-yoga, characterised by right vision, they come unto Me — they reach Me, the supreme Lord, who am their very Self, attaining Me as their own Self. Who? Those who, in the modes such as having their minds fixed in Me and the rest, worship Me.
BG_C10_V11: Out of compassion for those very ones, I, abiding in the seat of their inner being, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the luminous lamp of knowledge.
BG_C10_V11::block-0: When the question arises — for what purpose, and to whom, dost Thou give that buddhi-yoga which is the destroyer of the obstacles to attaining Thee, to those Thy devotees? — He says:
BG_C10_V11::block-1:
"Of those very ones (teṣām eva)" — out of compassion (anukampā-artham), namely, from the motive of mercy, with the thought "How indeed may welfare arise for them?" — I destroy the darkness, the gloom of delusion characterised as false cognition, born of ignorance (ajñāna-jam), that is, sprung from non-discrimination (avivekataḥ jātam).

Abiding in the seat of the Self (ātma-bhāva-sthaḥ): the bhāva of the ātman is the abode that is the inner instrument (antaḥkaraṇa-āśayaḥ); remaining established in that very seat, [I destroy it] by the lamp of knowledge (jñāna-dīpena), namely, by [a lamp] whose form is the cognition of discrimination (viveka-pratyaya-rūpeṇa), drenched with the oil of the affection of the grace of devotion (bhakti-prasāda-sneha-abhiṣiktena), fanned by the wind of intent application to meditation upon Me (mad-bhāvanā-abhiniveśa-vāta-īritena), having for its wick a wisdom refined by the disciplines of brahmacarya and the rest (brahmacarya-ādi-sādhana-saṃskāravat-prajñā-vartinā), supported by an inner organ free of attachment (virakta-antaḥkaraṇa-ādhāreṇa), set in a wind-still chamber that is a mind withdrawn from sense-objects and unsoiled by attachment and aversion (viṣaya-vyāvṛtta-citta-rāga-dveṣa-akaluṣita-nivāta-apavaraka-sthena), and shining with the right vision born of perpetually flowing one-pointed meditation (nitya-pravṛtta-aikāgrya-dhyāna-janita-samyag-darśana-bhāsvatā) — by such a lamp of knowledge, this is the meaning.
BG_C10_V12::block-0: Having heard the Lord's vibhūti and yoga as thus declared, Arjuna said:
BG_C10_V12::block-1: "The supreme Brahman, the supreme Self, the supreme abode, the supreme Light, the holy, the purifier, the supreme — the most pre-eminent — art Thou. The eternal Person, the everlasting, the divine — born in the heaven (divi bhavam) — the primal Deity (ādi-deva) of all the gods, that is, born at the beginning (ādau bhavam ādi-devam); the unborn, the all-pervading (vibhu), of the nature of pervading manifestation (vibhavana-śīlam).
BG_C10_V13: All the ṛṣis declare Thee thus, and so does the divine sage Nārada; Asita, Devala, and Vyāsa likewise; and Thou Thyself dost tell me so.
BG_C10_V13::block-1: They declare (āhuḥ), they speak of Thee — the ṛṣis, Vasiṣṭha and the rest, all of them; and the deva-ṛṣi Nārada likewise. Asita, and Devala too, says the very same; and Vyāsa as well; and Thou Thyself dost tell it to me.
BG_C10_V14: All this which Thou tellest me, O Keśava, I deem to be the truth; for, O Lord, neither the gods nor the dānavas know Thy manifestation.
BG_C10_V14::block-0: All this — that has thus been declared by the ṛṣis and by Thee — this I deem to be ṛta, that is, simply true (satyam eva), what Thou speakest, that Thou utterest, to me, O Keśava. For (hi), O Lord, Thy vyakti, that is, Thy origination (prabhavam), neither the gods know, nor the dānavas.
BG_C10_V15: Thou Thyself, by Thyself, knowest Thyself, O Supreme Person, O Source of beings, O Lord of beings, O God of gods, O Lord of the world.
BG_C10_V15::block-0: Since Thou art the origin of the gods and the rest, therefore —
BG_C10_V15::block-1: Thou Thyself alone (svayam eva), by Thyself (ātmanā), knowest Thyself (ātmānaṃ vetsi) — possessed of unsurpassed powers of knowledge, sovereignty, strength, and the rest, the Lord, O Puruṣottama. "He who brings forth (bhāvayati) beings" is bhūta-bhāvana — O Source of beings. O Bhūteśa — Lord of beings. O God of gods, O Lord of the world.
BG_C10_V16: Thou alone art able to declare, without remainder, those Thy divine self-glories by which Thou abidest pervading these worlds.
BG_C10_V16::block-0: Thou art able to declare (vaktum arhasi), to speak forth, without remainder (aśeṣeṇa). For divine indeed are the self-glories (ātma-vibhūtayaḥ); the vibhūtis of the Self — those Thou art able to declare. By those vibhūtis, that is, by those expanded glories of Thine own greatness (ātmano māhātmya-vistaraiḥ), Thou abidest pervading these worlds.
BG_C10_V17: How shall I, O Yogin, know Thee by ever meditating upon Thee? And in which and which forms art Thou, O Lord, to be contemplated by me?
BG_C10_V17::block-0: How shall I know (vidyām), how shall I come to recognise, Thee, O Yogin, ever meditating (sadā paricintayan) upon Thee? And in which and which forms (keṣu keṣu bhāveṣu), that is, in what objects (vastuṣu), art Thou to be contemplated (cintyaḥ asi), to be meditated upon (dhyeyaḥ asi), O Lord, by me?
BG_C10_V18: In detail, O Janārdana, tell once again Thy yoga and Thy vibhūti; for there is no satiety to me as I hear the immortal nectar [of Thy speech].
BG_C10_V18::block-0: In detail (vistareṇa), tell again Thy yoga, that is, the special might of yogic sovereignty (yoga-aiśvarya-śakti-viśeṣam), and Thy vibhūti, that is, the elaboration of the objects of meditation (dhyeya-padārthānāṃ vistaram), O Janārdana. The form is from the root ard whose meaning is motion: because of His causing the asuras, who are the adversaries of the gods, to go to the hells and the like (naraka-ādi-gamayitṛtvāt), He is Janārdana; or because He is besought (yācyate) by all people (sarvaiḥ janaiḥ) for the goals of human life — prosperity (abhyudaya) and the highest good (niḥśreyasa). Tell again (bhūyaḥ) what has already been declared before; for (hi) there is no tṛpti, no satisfaction, to me as I hear the nectar of words flowing forth from Thy mouth.
BG_C10_V19::block-0:
Now then (hanta), I shall recount to you those divine (divyāḥ — divi bhavāḥ, born in the celestial realm) self-glories of mine — the ātma-vibhūtis, that is, the manifestations of Myself, the Lord. The compound ātma-vibhūtayaḥ is unfolded as 'My own glories'. I shall declare them by way of pre-eminence (prādhānyataḥ): wherever a particular glory stands chief, that chief one I shall narrate as foremost, O best of the Kurus. To recount them in their entirety (aśeṣataḥ), however, is not possible even in a hundred years; for, says the Lord, there is no end to the extent (vistara) of My glories. This is the purport.

Thus the upakrama of the discourse on vibhūti is laid down: pre-eminent instances will be named, while infinitude is conceded — the very mark of Īśvara's aiśvarya.
BG_C10_V20: I am the Self, O Guḍākeśa, seated in the heart of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and the very end of beings.
BG_C10_V20::block-0: Among them, hear first of all this —
BG_C10_V20::block-1:
I am the Ātman — the inner Self (pratyag-ātman). 'Guḍākeśa': guḍākā is sleep, and the lord (īśa) of that is Guḍākeśa — one who has conquered sleep (jita-nidraḥ); or alternatively, 'thick-haired' (ghana-keśa). The vigraha is given in both forms; Śaṅkara prefers the first sense as more apt to the address of the awakened seeker.

'Seated in the āśaya (the inner heart) of all beings' — I, the Self, the inmost Self, am ever to be meditated upon (nityaṁ dhyeyaḥ) by him who is competent for the contemplation of the Self. And by one who is unequal to that, I am to be contemplated in the subsequent manifestations (the vibhūtis hereafter to be named); for it is I alone who am the beginning of beings — that is, their cause (kāraṇam) — and likewise the middle, that is, their continued existence (sthitiḥ), and the end, that is, their dissolution (pralayaḥ).

Thus a graded upāsanā is taught: the foremost course is direct meditation on the pratyag-ātman seated in the heart; the secondary course, for those of lesser capacity, is meditation on the Lord through His vibhūtis.
BG_C10_V21: Among the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; among lights, the radiant Sun; among the Maruts I am Marīci; among the constellations I am the Moon.
BG_C10_V21::block-0: And it is in this manner that I am to be meditated upon —
BG_C10_V21::block-1: Among the twelve Ādityas, I am the one named Viṣṇu. Among lights — that is, among the illuminators (prakāśayitṝṇām) — I am the Sun (ravi), the bearer of rays (aṁśumān, raśmimān). Among the Maruts — the divisions of the Marut deities — I am the one called Marīci. Among the nakṣatras (constellations / lunar mansions) I am the Moon (śaśin, candramas).
BG_C10_V22: Among the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; among the gods I am Vāsava (Indra); among the senses I am the mind; in beings I am consciousness.
BG_C10_V22::block-0:
Among the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda. Among the gods — Rudras, Ādityas and the rest — I am Vāsava, that is, Indra. Of the eleven senses (the eye and the others) I am also the mind (manas), of the nature of saṅkalpa-vikalpa (resolution and doubt).

'In beings I am consciousness (cetanā)' — within the assemblage of body and instruments (kārya-karaṇa-saṅghāta), the perpetually manifest function of the buddhi is what is called cetanā; that I am. Note that Śaṅkara explains cetanā here as the buddhi-vṛtti ever-evident in the psycho-physical complex, not as the witnessing Self spoken of earlier; for the Self has already been declared in verse 20, and what is being enumerated now is His vibhūti within manifest beings.
BG_C10_V23: Among the Rudras I am Śaṅkara; of yakṣas and rākṣasas, the Lord of wealth (Kubera); among the Vasus I am Pāvaka (Fire); among the peaked mountains, Meru.
BG_C10_V23::block-0: Among the eleven Rudras I am also Śaṅkara. Vitteśa — the lord of wealth, Kubera — I am, of the yakṣas and the rākṣasas. Among the eight Vasus I am also Pāvaka, that is, Agni. Among śikharins — those possessed of peaks (śikhara-vat) — I am Meru.
BG_C10_V24: Among household priests, O Pārtha, know Me to be the chief — Bṛhaspati; among generals I am Skanda; among waters I am the ocean.
BG_C10_V24::block-0:
Among purodhāḥ — that is, royal household-priests (rāja-purohita) — know Me, O Pārtha, to be the chief, the foremost: Bṛhaspati. For he, being Indra's purohita, must indeed be the chief of purohitas. Among senānīs — leaders of armies, generals — I am Skanda, the commander of the celestial host. Among saras — those reservoirs of water dug by the gods themselves (deva-khāta-saraḥ) — I am Sāgara, the ocean: this I am, this I become.

By reading 'saras' here as 'natural, god-fashioned reservoirs', Śaṅkara saves the verse from the apparent oddity of placing the ocean among small lakes; the comparison is among the great primordial bodies of water.
BG_C10_V25: Among the great seers I am Bhṛgu; among utterances I am the single syllable (Oṁ); among sacrifices I am the japa-yajña; among things that stand fast, the Himālaya.
BG_C10_V25::block-0:
Among the great ṛṣis I am Bhṛgu. Among utterances (girām, vācām) — taken in the form of words (pada-lakṣaṇānām) — I am the one indestructible syllable, the Oṁkāra. Among yajñas I am the japa-yajña; among the standing ones — the immovable, those that abide in fixity (sthiti-mat) — I am the Himālaya.

The choice of japa-yajña among sacrifices and Oṁkāra among words discloses the inner thrust of the chapter: the Lord highlights the means most directly conducive to vidyā and mokṣa, since 'yajñānāṁ japa-yajño'smi' is itself an upāsanā-praising vibhūti.
BG_C10_V26: Of all trees the Aśvattha; of divine seers, Nārada; among gandharvas Citraratha; among the perfected ones, the sage Kapila.
BG_C10_V26::block-0:
Of all trees, the Aśvattha. Of deva-ṛṣis: gods who, while remaining gods, attained the status of ṛṣis by virtue of being mantra-seers (mantra-darśitvāt) are the deva-ṛṣis; of them I am Nārada. The samāsa-vigraha is given thus: 'devāḥ eva santaḥ ṛṣitvaṁ prāptāḥ — those who, being themselves gods, have attained ṛṣi-hood'.

Of the gandharvas I am the gandharva named Citraratha. Of siddhas — those who, by their very birth (janmanā eva), have attained the surpassing excellence of dharma, jñāna, vairāgya and aiśvarya — I am the sage Kapila.

Note: Śaṅkara here intends Kapila the siddha-muni endowed with the four-fold pre-eminence; this is by no means an endorsement of the Sāṅkhya doctrine of an independent prakṛti — that school the bhāṣya elsewhere refutes, holding all vibhūti to rest in Īśvara alone.
BG_C10_V27: Among horses, know Me to be Uccaiḥśravas, born of nectar; among elephant-lords, Airāvata; and among men, the king of men.
BG_C10_V27::block-0: Among horses (aśvānām), Uccaiḥśravas — that horse-king of that name — know Me to be him; comprehend Me as that one, born of nectar (amṛtodbhavam), that is, sprung up on the occasion of the churning for nectar. Airāvata — the offspring of Irāvatī — among the lords of elephants (gajendrāṇām), the chiefs of pachyderms; with regard to him also, the phrase 'know Me to be' is carried over by anuvṛtti. And among men (narāṇām), that is, among human beings, know Me, comprehend Me, to be the king (narādhipam) — their sovereign.
BG_C10_V28: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am Kāmadhuk; I am the progenitor Kandarpa; among serpents I am Vāsuki.
BG_C10_V28::block-0: Of weapons (āyudhānām) I am the thunderbolt (vajram), the one fashioned out of the bones of Dadhīci. Among milch-cows (dhenūnām), the yielders of milk, I am Kāmadhuk — Vasiṣṭha's cow, the yielder of every wish; or else, the cow that yields desires generically. I am the progenitor (prajanaḥ), the one who brings forth offspring — namely Kandarpa, the god of desire. Among serpents (sarpāṇām), the various species of snakes, I am Vāsuki, the king of serpents.
BG_C10_V29: Among Nāgas I am Ananta; of water-creatures I am Varuṇa; among the Pitṛs I am Aryaman; and of those who restrain, I am Yama.
BG_C10_V29::block-0: And I am Ananta among the Nāgas (nāgānām), the special class of serpents — that is, I am the king of the Nāgas. I am Varuṇa among the water-creatures (yādasām) — the king of the water-deities. Among the Pitṛs I am the one named Aryaman — the king of the Pitṛs. And of those who exercise restraint and chastisement (saṃyamatām), who carry out the act of binding and judging, I am Yama.
BG_C10_V30: Among Daityas I am Prahlāda; among reckoners I am Time; among beasts I am the king of beasts; and among birds I am the son of Vinatā.
BG_C10_V30::block-0: And I am the one named Prahlāda among the Daityas, the descendants of Diti's line. Among reckoners (kalayatām) — those who carry out kalanā, that is, counting, computation — I am Time (kālaḥ). And among beasts (mṛgāṇām) I am the king of beasts (mṛgendraḥ), namely the lion or the tiger. And I am Vainateya — Garutmān, the son of Vinatā — among the birds (pakṣiṇām), the winged ones (patatriṇām).
BG_C10_V31: Of purifiers I am the wind; of weapon-bearers I am Rāma; among fishes I am the makara; and of streams I am the Jāhnavī.
BG_C10_V31::block-0: Of those that purify (pavatām), of purifiers, I am the wind (pavanaḥ), namely the air. I am Rāma among weapon-bearers (śastra-bhṛtām), among the wielders of arms — the Rāma here is Rāma the son of Daśaratha; that Rāma am I. Among fishes (jhaṣāṇām) — among matsyas and the like — I am the particular species named makara. And of streams, of flowing rivers (sravantīnām), I am the Jāhnavī, the Gaṅgā.
BG_C10_V32: Of creations I am the beginning, the end and the middle, O Arjuna; among sciences I am the science of the Self; of disputants I am the dialectic.
BG_C10_V32::block-0:
Of creations (sargāṇām), of bringings-forth, I am the beginning (ādi), the end (anta) and indeed the middle (madhya) — that is, I am the origination, sustenance and dissolution, O Arjuna. At the very outset of this glory-section it was said that of beings ensouled by living principles I am the beginning and the end and so forth; here, however, it is the totality of every kind of creation as such — that is the distinction here.

The science of the Self (adhyātma-vidyā) — among sciences (vidyānām) — is foremost (pradhānam) on account of its tending to liberation (mokṣārthatvāt); that I am. Disputation (vādaḥ) is the chief among the speeches of disputants (pravadatām), since it is the means of arriving at the determination of meaning (artha-nirṇaya-hetutvāt); therefore that I am. By way of the agent of speaking — that is, by mention of the speakers — only the species of speech, namely vāda, jalpa, and vitaṇḍā, are taken up here under the term 'pravadatām'.
BG_C10_V33: Of letters I am the A; of compounds I am the dvandva; I alone am imperishable Time; I am the Dispenser facing every direction.
BG_C10_V33::block-0:
Among letters (akṣarāṇām), among the syllabic sounds, I am the letter A. The dvandva (the copulative compound) is the compound that I am, among the totality of compounds (sāmāsikasya), that is, the assemblage of all kinds of samāsa.

Further, I myself am the imperishable Time (akṣayaḥ kālaḥ) — the unspent — that well-known Time which goes by the names of kṣaṇa and the rest; or else, the supreme Lord who is the Time even of Time. I am the Dispenser (dhātā), the ordainer of the fruits of action for the entire world, facing every direction (viśvatomukhaḥ) — that is, sarvatomukha, having faces on every side.
BG_C10_V34: I am all-snatching Death, and the rise of those who shall come to be; and among feminine qualities I am Fame, Fortune, Speech, Memory, Intelligence, Constancy and Forbearance.
BG_C10_V34::block-0:
Death is of two kinds: that which carries off wealth and the like, and that which carries off the life-breath; of these, that which carries off the life-breath is called the all-snatcher (sarva-haraḥ); that am I — this is the meaning. Or else, the supreme Lord, on account of carrying off everything at the dissolution, is the all-snatcher; that am I.

Udbhava (rise) means upraising, exaltation, prosperity; and I am the cause of attaining it. For whom? Of bhaviṣyatām — of those whose welfare is to come, those who are fit for the attainment of exaltation — this is the meaning.

Fame (kīrti), Fortune (śrī), Speech (vāk), Memory (smṛti), Intelligence (medhā), Constancy (dhṛti) and Forbearance (kṣamā) — these excellent attributes among women am I; with even the slightest semblance of connection with which the world deems itself fulfilled.
BG_C10_V35: Of the Sāmans I am the Bṛhat-sāman, of the meters the Gāyatrī; of the months I am Mārgaśīrṣa, of the seasons the flower-bearer (spring).
BG_C10_V35::block-0: Of the Sāmans, I am the Bṛhat-sāman, the foremost. "Gāyatrī of the meters": among the ṛks distinguished by meters such as gāyatrī, etc., I am that ṛk which is set in the gāyatrī meter — this is the meaning. Of the months I am Mārgaśīrṣa; of the seasons I am the flower-bearer, namely spring (vasanta).
BG_C10_V36: Of the deceitful I am gambling; I am the brilliance of the brilliant. I am victory, I am resolve; I am the sattva of those endowed with sattva.
BG_C10_V36::block-0: Of those who deceive — that is, of the doers of deception — I am gambling, characterised by dice-play and the like. I am the brilliance (tejas) of the brilliant. I am the victory of victors; I am the resolve (vyavasāya) of the resolute; I am the sattva — the sattva-quality — of those endowed with sattva, that is, of the sāttvika ones.
BG_C10_V37: Of the Vṛṣṇis I am Vāsudeva; of the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya. Of munis I am Vyāsa; of the seer-poets, Uśanas the kavi.
BG_C10_V37::block-0: Of the Vṛṣṇis — that is, of the Yādavas — I am Vāsudeva; this very one am I, your friend. Of the Pāṇḍavas, Dhanañjaya —
BG_C10_V37::block-1: you yourself. Of munis — those whose nature is reflection (manana), the knowers of all things — I am Vyāsa; of the kavis, the seers of remote vision (krāntadarśins), I am Uśanas the kavi.
BG_C10_V38: Of those who chastise I am the rod (daṇḍa); of those seeking conquest I am right-policy (nīti). Of secrets I am silence; I am the knowledge of the knowers.
BG_C10_V38::block-0: Of the chastisers — those who subdue — I am the rod, the means of subduing the unsubdued. I am the right-policy (nīti) of those seeking to conquer, of those who wish to be victorious. And of secrets — of things to be guarded — I am silence (mauna). I am the knowledge of those endowed with knowledge.
BG_C10_V39: And whatever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O Arjuna. There is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist apart from Me.
BG_C10_V39::block-0:
And whatever is the seed of all beings — the cause of their sprouting forth — that am I, O Arjuna.

In order to bring the topic to a close, He states the summary of His vibhūtis (manifold majesties): there is no being, moving or unmoving, that could exist apart from Me. For when severed, abandoned, by Me, that being would be devoid of self, void — a mere blank. Hence the meaning is: all this has Me for its very Self (mad-ātmaka).
BG_C10_V40: There is no end to My divine vibhūtis, O scorcher of foes. This expanse of vibhūti has been spoken by Me only by way of indication.
BG_C10_V40::block-0: There is no end to the expanses of My divine vibhūtis, O scorcher of foes. For of the Lord, who is the Self of all, the measure of the divine vibhūtis is incapable of being spoken or known by anyone whatsoever. But this expanse of vibhūti has been spoken by Me only by way of indication, that is, partially, touching only one portion.
BG_C10_V41: Whatever existent is endowed with vibhūti, prosperous, or invigorated — know that very thing as having arisen from a fragment of My splendour.
BG_C10_V41::block-0: Whatever entity in the world is possessed of vibhūti — endowed with majesty — or is śrīmat, accompanied by Śrī (Lakṣmī, prosperity), or is ūrjita, endowed with vigour — that very thing know thou, comprehend, as tejo-aṁśa-sambhava: that of which the origin is one fragment, one portion, of the splendour of Me, the Lord. Thus understand it.
BG_C10_V42: Or rather, what is gained, Arjuna, by your knowing all this in detail? With a single fragment of Myself I stand, sustaining this entire universe.
BG_C10_V42::block-0:
Or rather, what gain, Arjuna, would there be for you in this much being known — in such partial knowledge that still leaves a remainder? Hear instead the meaning that is being declared without remainder: viṣṭabhya — having firmly fixed, having made it stand fast — this entire universe, ekāṁśena — by one part, one limb, one foot — that is, in the form of all beings.

And accordingly the mantra-text declares: "One foot of Him is all beings" (Ṛk-saṃhitā 10.8.90.3) — sthitaḥ aham, thus do I stand.
BG_C11_V01::block-0: The Lord's vibhūtis (manifestations of glory) have been declared. Therein, having heard the Lord's pronouncement, 'Pervading this entire universe with a single fragment of Myself I abide' (Bh. Gī. 10.42), Arjuna, desiring to behold directly that primordial sovereign form which is the very Self of the universe, said —
BG_C11_V01::block-1: 'For My favour' (madanugrahāya) — for the sake of bestowing grace upon me; the supreme — that is, unsurpassable; secret — meaning what is to be kept hidden; designated as adhyātma — having for its province the discrimination between the Self (Ātman) and the not-Self; that utterance, that statement, which has been spoken by Thee — by that statement of Thine this delusion of mine has departed; the import being that my non-discriminating cognition has been driven away. ||1||
BG_C11_V02: For the origin and dissolution of beings have been heard by me from Thee in detail, O lotus-petal-eyed one, and likewise Thy imperishable greatness. ||2||
BG_C11_V02::block-1: Bhava — origination; apyaya — dissolution; these two, the bhavāpyayau of beings, have been heard, indeed, by me in detail (vistaraśaḥ), not in summary, from Thee — that is, in Thy presence. 'Lotus-petal-eyed' — the petal of a lotus is kamalapatra; he whose two eyes are like that, that is Thou; the compound is vigraha thus: kamalapatre iva akṣiṇī yasya = kamalapatrākṣaḥ; O lotus-petal-eyed one. The state of being mahātman is māhātmya — Thy greatness too, which is imperishable, undecaying — here the word 'heard' (śrutam) carries over by anuvṛtti. ||2||
BG_C11_V03: So is this, even as Thou hast Thyself declared concerning Thyself, O Supreme Lord. I desire to behold Thy sovereign form, O Best of Persons. ||3||
BG_C11_V03::block-0: It is thus, not otherwise, in the manner in which Thou speakest of Thyself, O Supreme Lord. Yet even so I desire to behold that sovereign form of Thine — endowed with knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, valour, and effulgence — that Vaiṣṇava form, O Best of Persons (Puruṣottama). ||3||
BG_C11_V04: If Thou deemest, O Lord, that it can be beheld by me, then, O Master of Yoga, do Thou show me Thy imperishable Self. ||4||
BG_C11_V04::block-0: If Thou deemest — that is, considerest — that it (that form) is capable of being beheld by me, by Arjuna, O Lord (prabho), O Master; 'Yogeśvara' — the yogas belong to the yogins, and their lord is the yogeśvara; O Lord of Yoga. Since I am exceedingly desirous of beholding, therefore, on that account, do Thou show — for my sake — Thy imperishable Self. ||4||
BG_C11_V05::block-0: Being thus urged by Arjuna, the Lord said —
BG_C11_V05::block-1: Behold, O Pārtha, My forms by hundreds and by thousands — the meaning is, manifold (many-fold). And these are nānāvidhāni — of many kinds; divi bhavāni — divya — divine, that is, supra-natural (non-prākṛta); and nānāvarṇākṛtīni — having various varieties of colour and shape: the various, that is, distinct, modes such as blue, yellow, and so forth, are varṇas; and likewise the ākṛtis — the particular configurations of limbs — of which forms; thus 'nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca'. ||5||
BG_C11_V06: Behold the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Aśvins, and likewise the Maruts; behold, O scion of Bharata, many marvels never before seen. ||6||
BG_C11_V06::block-0: Behold the Ādityas — twelve in number; the Vasus — eight; the Rudras — eleven; the two Aśvins; the Maruts — those who are seven groups of seven each. Likewise behold many other marvels too, never before seen by thee in the human world — neither by thee nor by any other than thee — wonders, astonishing things, O scion of Bharata. ||6||
BG_C11_V07: Behold today, O Guḍākeśa, the entire universe, with its moving and unmoving, gathered together in one place — here in My body — and whatever else thou desirest to see. ||7||
BG_C11_V07::block-1: Iha — here, ekastham — abiding in one place; the entire universe, the whole of it, behold today (now), with its moving and unmoving — that which subsists together with the moving (cara) and the unmoving (acara) — in My body, O Guḍākeśa. And whatever else — victory, defeat, and the like — about which thou hast misgiving, that which thou didst utter, 'Whether we should conquer them or whether they should conquer us' (Bh. Gī. 2.6) — that too, if thou desirest to behold. ||7||
BG_C11_V08: But thou art not able to behold Me with this thine own eye; I bestow on thee the divine eye — behold My sovereign yoga. ||8||
BG_C11_V08::block-1: But thou art not able to behold Me — bearing the universal form — with this very prākṛta (natural, ordinary) eye, with thine own eye. The eye, however, with which thou shalt be able to behold — that is divine; that divine eye I bestow upon thee. With it behold My sovereign yoga (yogam aiśvaram) — the yoga of Myself the Lord, that is, the supreme display of yogic power. ||8||
BG_C11_V09::block-0: Having spoken thus, in the manner just stated, then, immediately afterwards, O King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the great Lord of yoga — He who is great and who is at once the Lord of yoga, namely Hari, Nārāyaṇa — showed, that is, displayed, to Pārtha, the son of Pṛthā, His supreme form, the universal form (viśva-rūpa), the form belonging to the Lord (aiśvaram).
BG_C11_V10: With many mouths and eyes, with many wondrous sights to behold, with many divine ornaments, with many divine uplifted weapons. (10)
BG_C11_V10::block-0: Aneka-vaktra-nayanam — that form in which there are many (aneka) mouths (vaktra) and eyes (nayana) is aneka-vaktra-nayanam. Aneka-adbhuta-darśanam — that form in which there are many (aneka) wondrous (adbhuta), that is, astonishing, sights (darśana) is the form aneka-adbhuta-darśanam. Likewise aneka-divya-ābharaṇam — that in which there are many (aneka) divine (divya) ornaments (ābharaṇa) is aneka-divya-ābharaṇam. Likewise divya-aneka-udyata-āyudham — that in which there are many (aneka) divine (divya) weapons (āyudha) such as the sword and the rest, held uplifted (udyata), is divya-aneka-udyata-āyudham. The connection with the previous word ‘darśayāmāsa’ (showed) is to be supplied.
BG_C11_V11: Wearing divine garlands and garments, anointed with divine fragrant unguents, made up of all marvels, the resplendent, infinite One whose face is turned everywhere. (11)
BG_C11_V11::block-1: Divya-mālya-ambara-dharam — that Lord by whom divine (divya) garlands (mālya), namely flowers, and garments (ambara), namely cloths, are worn (dhriyante) is divya-mālya-ambara-dharam — Him. Divya-gandha-anulepanam — He whose anointment with fragrant paste (gandha-anulepana) is divine (divya) is divya-gandha-anulepanam — Him. Sarva-āścarya-mayam — composed almost wholly of all marvels (sarva-āścarya-prāya). The deva (resplendent One). Anantam — He of whom there exists no end (anta) is ananta — Him. Viśvato-mukham — having faces (mukha) on every side (sarvataḥ), since He is the very Self of all beings (sarva-bhūta-ātma-bhūtatvāt) — Him He showed. Or alternatively, the words ‘arjunaḥ dadarśa’ (Arjuna saw) may be supplied.
BG_C11_V12: If, in the sky, the radiance of a thousand suns risen simultaneously were to be there, that radiance might perhaps be like the radiance of that great-souled One. (12)
BG_C11_V12::block-0: Now, regarding the radiance of the Lord in His universal form, an analogy is given —
BG_C11_V12::block-1: Divi — in the intermediate sky, or else in the third heaven; sūryāṇāṁ sahasram — sūrya-sahasra, a thousand suns; the radiance (bhāḥ) of that thousand suns risen simultaneously, the radiance of that simultaneously risen thousand suns — that radiance, were it (yadi) to be, might (syāt) be like (sadṛśī) the radiance of that great-souled One Himself, that is, of the universal form. Or, were it not so, then the radiance of the universal form alone exceeds it — this is the purport.
BG_C11_V13: There, in the body of the God of gods, the son of Pāṇḍu then beheld the entire universe, abiding in one place, divided into many. (13)
BG_C11_V13::block-1: Tatra, in that one universal form, eka-stham — abiding (sthitam) in one (eka) place — the entire (kṛtsnam) universe (jagat), divided (pravibhaktam) in many ways (anekadhā), through the distinctions of gods, ancestors, men and the rest (deva-pitṛ-manuṣya-ādi-bhedaiḥ) — apaśyat, saw, that is, beheld; in the body (śarīre) of the God of gods (deva-deva), namely Hari; the son of Pāṇḍu (pāṇḍava), Arjuna; tadā, then.
BG_C11_V14: Then he, Dhanañjaya, filled with wonder and with hair standing on end, bowing his head before the Lord, with palms joined, spoke. (14)
BG_C11_V14::block-0: Tataḥ — thereafter, having seen Him, that one, namely Dhanañjaya, became filled with wonder (vismaya-āviṣṭa) — pervaded by wonder (vismayena āviṣṭaḥ) — and one whose hair stood on end (hṛṣṭa-romā) — he in whom the hairs (romāṇi) were thrilled and erect (hṛṣṭāni). Praṇamya — having bowed deeply, that is, having performed prostration in a pre-eminent manner, becoming bent low, with the head (śirasā), before the Lord (devam) who bore the universal form, kṛta-añjaliḥ — with hands cupped together for the purpose of salutation — he abhāṣata, that is, spoke.
BG_C11_V15::block-0: How? — Disclosing his own experience by saying, “What universal form has been shown by Thee, that I see,” Arjuna said —
BG_C11_V15::block-1: Paśyāmi — I see, that is, I apprehend; O Deva, in Thy body all the gods (devān sarvān); likewise the hosts of distinctive beings (bhūta-viśeṣa-saṅghān) — the hosts (saṅgha) of distinctive beings (bhūta-viśeṣa), namely of the immobile and mobile creatures (sthāvara-jaṅgama) of various structural distinctions (nānā-saṁsthāna-viśeṣa) — those hosts. Furthermore — Brahmā, the four-faced one, the Lord (īśam), the ruler of creatures (prajānām īśitāram), seated upon a lotus (kamala-āsana-stham); the meaning is, seated upon the pericarp of Mount Meru in the middle of the earth-lotus. And the seers (ṛṣīn), Vasiṣṭha and the rest, all of them; and the serpents (uragān), Vāsuki and the others, divine (divyān) — those existing in heaven (divi).
BG_C11_V16: I behold Thee, possessed of many arms, bellies, mouths, and eyes, of infinite forms on every side. I see no end, no middle, nor again any beginning of Thee, O Lord of the universe, O universal form. (16)
BG_C11_V16::block-0: Aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netram — He of whom Thou art such, namely Thou, in whom there are many (aneka) arms (bāhu), bellies (udara), mouths (vaktra), and eyes (netra), is aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netraḥ — Thee who art aneka-bāhu-udara-vaktra-netram. Paśyāmi tvā — I see Thee; sarvataḥ — everywhere, on every side; ananta-rūpam — He whose forms (rūpa) are infinite (ananta) is ananta-rūpaḥ — Thee who art ananta-rūpam. Na antam — no end, that is, no termination; na madhyam — no middle, ‘middle’ being that which is between two extremities (kotī); na punaḥ tava ādim — nor again Thy beginning. The sense is: I see no end of the deva, I see no middle, nor again do I see any beginning, O Viśveśvara (Lord of the universe), O Viśva-rūpa (universal form).
BG_C11_V17: I behold You wearing the diadem, bearing the mace and the discus — a mass of effulgence blazing on every side, hard to gaze upon, illumined all around with the radiance of blazing fire and the sun, immeasurable.
BG_C11_V17::block-1:
"Diademed" — kirīṭa is a particular ornament worn upon the head; he by whom it is borne is kirīṭī, and Him I behold as kirīṭinam. Likewise "mace-bearing" — gadā is His, hence gadī, and Him as gadinam. So too "discus-wielding" — the cakra is His, hence cakrī, and Him as cakriṇam. "A mass of effulgence" (tejorāśim) — a heap of brilliance; "radiating on every side" (sarvatodīptimantam) — He in whom the shining-forth is on every side is sarvatodīptimān, and Him as such I behold.

"You" — "hard to look upon" (durnirīkṣyam) — He who is gazed upon only with difficulty is durnirīkṣya, and Him as such. "On every side" (samantāt) means everywhere. "With the splendor of blazing fire and sun" — fire and sun are anala and arka; both blazing are dīptānalārkau; the dīpti, the lustre, that is as the lustre of those two blazing ones — He whose tejas is such is dīptānalārkadyutiḥ, and Him as such (dīptānalārkadyutim) do I behold. "Immeasurable" (aprameyam) — not an object of measurement, that is, incapable of being delimited.
BG_C11_V18: You are the supreme Imperishable, the One to be known; You are the highest resting-place of this whole universe. You are the undecaying guardian of the eternal Dharma; You, I hold, are the Sanātana Puruṣa.
BG_C11_V18::block-0: From this very seeing of Your yoga-power I infer —
BG_C11_V18::block-1: "You are akṣaram" — that which does not perish — the supreme Brahman, to be known by those who seek liberation. "You are the supreme nidhāna of this whole world" — that in which it is laid down (nidhīyate asmin), the supreme refuge — that is the meaning. Further, "You are avyaya" — He in whom no decay (vyaya) exists is avyaya. "Guardian of the eternal Dharma" (śāśvatadharmagoptā) — the Dharma which abides ever (śaśvadbhavaḥ), eternal, perpetual; its protector is śāśvatadharmagoptā. "Sanātana" — primordial, from of old. You are the Puruṣa, the supreme — such is My (mama, Arjuna's) considered conviction.
BG_C11_V19: Without beginning, middle or end, of infinite valor, infinite-armed, with the moon and sun for eyes, blazing fire as Your mouth — I behold You scorching this whole universe with Your own splendor.
BG_C11_V19::block-1:
"Anādimadhyāntam" — He of whom there is no beginning (ādi), no middle (madhya), no end (anta) is anādimadhyānta; You as such. "Anantavīryam" — He of whose vīrya there is no end is anantavīrya; You as such. So too "infinite-armed" — He whose arms are endless is anantabāhu; You as such. "Śaśisūryanetram" — He whose two eyes are the moon and the sun is śaśisūryanetra; You as such — having moon and sun for eyes.

I behold You — "with blazing-fire mouths" (dīptahutāśavaktram) — He whose mouth is the blazing oblation-eater (fire) is dīptahutāśavaktra; You as such — "by Your own tejas burning this entire universe (viśvam idaṁ samastam tapantam)."
BG_C11_V20: This space between heaven and earth, and all the quarters, are pervaded by You alone; seeing this Your wonderful, terrible form, the three worlds shudder, O Mahātman.
BG_C11_V20::block-0: "This antaram between heaven and earth" — that is, the intermediate sky — "is pervaded by You alone," the bearer of the cosmic form, and so too "all the quarters" are pervaded. "Having seen" — having beheld — "this wonderful (adbhutam)," astounding, "form of Yours, fierce (ugram), cruel," the three worlds — the triad of worlds — are "prav-yathitam," terrified, made to tremble, O Mahātman, You whose nature is no petty thing (akṣudrasvabhāva).
BG_C11_V21: These hosts of gods enter into You; some, frightened, with folded hands extol You; bands of great seers and perfected ones, exclaiming "May it be well!", praise You with full and ample hymns.
BG_C11_V21::block-0: Now, in order to settle that doubt of Arjuna's stated earlier — "whether we should conquer them or they should conquer us" (Gītā 2.6) — the Lord set forth, intent upon showing the certainty of the Pāṇḍavas' victory; seeing Him so engaged, Arjuna says — and further —
BG_C11_V21::block-1: "These" warring combatants — "hosts of gods" — those bands of Vasus and the rest who have descended here in human form to relieve the burden of the earth — "enter into You," are seen entering. Among them, "some, frightened, with añjali joined," extol You, since they are powerless even to flee. When the battle has come on, observing portents and other signs, exclaiming "May it be well with the world!" — "hosts of great seers and siddhas" — bands of maharṣis and siddhas — "praise You with full hymns" — with abundant, complete praises.
BG_C11_V22: The Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, those who are Sādhyas, the Viśve-devas, the two Aśvins, the Maruts and the steam-drinking Manes, the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras and Siddhas — all these gaze upon You, and all are struck with wonder.
BG_C11_V22::block-1: "The Rudras, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and those who are Sādhyas" — the troops of Rudras and the rest, the Viśve-devas, the two Aśvin gods, the Maruts and the "steam-drinkers" (ūṣmapāḥ), namely the Pitṛs; "hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras, and Siddhas" — Gandharvas such as Hāhā, Hūhū and the rest; Yakṣas such as Kubera and the rest; Asuras such as Virocana and the rest; Siddhas such as Kapila and the rest — their hosts make up the gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghāḥ. They all "behold You," struck with wonder, having become amazed — all of them just so.
BG_C11_V23: Seeing this great form of Yours with many mouths and eyes, O mighty-armed, with many arms, thighs and feet, with many bellies, terrible with many tusks — the worlds shudder, and so do I.
BG_C11_V23::block-1: "Your form" — vast in dimension, exceedingly large — "with many mouths and eyes" — that form in which there are many vaktras, mouths, and many netras, eyes, is bahuvaktranetram. O mighty-armed one — "bahubāhūrupādam" — that form in which there are many arms (bāhus), thighs (ūrus), and feet (pādas) is bahubāhūrupādam. Further, "with many bellies" — that in which there are many bellies (udaras) is bahūdaram. "Terrible with many tusks" — that which is fierce, distorted (vikṛtam), by many tusks (daṁṣṭrās) is bahudaṁṣṭrākarālam. Having seen such a form, the worlds — common, worldly creatures — are shuddering, sent into trembling by fear; and so also I.
BG_C11_V24: Touching the sky, blazing, of many hues, with mouths agape, with vast blazing eyes — having seen You so, my inmost being trembles, and I find no firmness nor peace, O Viṣṇu.
BG_C11_V24::block-1:
"Sky-touching" (nabhaḥsprśam) — touching the heaven; "blazing" — flaming; "of many hues" — He in whom are many colors, fearsome, of varied configurations, that You as anekavarṇam. "With gaping mouths" (vyāttānanam) — He in whom the mouths are open, parted, You as such. "With blazing, vast eyes" — He in whom the eyes are blazing, kindled, and broad, extended, You as dīptaviśālanetram.

Having seen You so, "prav-yathitāntarātmā" — he whose antarātman, mind, is shaken, fully terrified — being such, I do not find dhṛti, firmness, nor śama, calming, mental satisfaction, O Viṣṇu.
BG_C11_V25: Having seen Your mouths, terrible with tusks and resembling the fire of universal dissolution, I know not the directions, nor do I find ease. Be gracious, O Lord of gods, O Abode of the worlds! (25)
BG_C11_V25::block-1:
"Daṃṣṭrā-karālāni" — terrible, distorted (vikṛta) by reason of the tusks (daṃṣṭrās) — such are "te mukhāni," Your mouths. "Dṛṣṭvaiva" — merely upon perceiving them. "Kālānala-saṃnibhāni" — at the time of cosmic dissolution the fire that consumes the worlds is the kālānala; resembling that (tat-sadṛśāni) are these mouths, kālānala-saṃnibhāni — having beheld such mouths, this is meant.

"Diśo na jāne" — I am unable to discern the directions by way of distinguishing east from west; I have become bewildered as to the quarters (diṅ-mūḍha). Therefore, "na labhe ca śarma" — and I do not obtain (na upalabhe) ease, that is, happiness. Hence, "prasīda" — be gracious, become well-pleased, O Lord of the gods (Deveśa), O Abode of the worlds (Jagannivāsa).
BG_C11_V26: And these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, all of them, together with the hosts of kings; Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and that son of the charioteer (Karṇa) likewise, along with even our own foremost warriors — (26)
BG_C11_V26::block-0: The apprehension of defeat I had with respect to those (warriors) — that too has departed. Because —
BG_C11_V26::block-1: "And these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra" (amī ca tvāṃ Dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ) — Duryodhana and the rest — the syntactical connection is with the words occurring later, "hastening they enter" (tvaramāṇāḥ viśanti). "Sarve sahaiva" — all together, conjoined "with the hosts of avanipālas" — those who guard (pālayanti) the avani, that is, the earth, are avanipālas (kings); along with their hosts. Furthermore, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, the son of the charioteer (sūta-putra), namely Karṇa, and likewise that one — together with even our own — Dhṛṣṭadyumna and the rest — the foremost of warriors (yodha-mukhya), the chief, principal among the fighters.
BG_C11_V27: Hastening they enter Your mouths, terrible with tusks and frightful. Some are seen sticking in the gaps between Your teeth, with their heads ground to powder. (27)
BG_C11_V27::block-1: "Vaktrāṇi" — the mouths — "te," Your, "tvaramāṇāḥ" — being filled with haste — "viśanti," they enter. Of what description are these mouths? "Daṃṣṭrā-karālāni bhayānakāni" — terrible by reason of the tusks, frightful (bhayaṅkara). Furthermore, "kecit" — some among those that have entered the mouths — caught (vilagna) in the spaces between the teeth (daśanāntara) like flesh that has been eaten — "sandṛśyante," they are perceived, "cūrṇitaiḥ uttamāṅgaiḥ" — with their heads (uttamāṅga, śiras) reduced to powder (cūrṇī-kṛta).
BG_C11_V28: As the many torrents of water of rivers rush directly toward the ocean alone, so do these heroes of the world of men enter Your blazing mouths. (28)
BG_C11_V28::block-0: How do they enter the mouths? He says —
BG_C11_V28::block-1: "Yathā" — just as — of the rivers (nadī, sravantī), "bahavaḥ" — many — "ambu-vegāḥ" — torrents of water, particular speeds (tvarā-viśeṣa) — flow toward (drava, viśanti) the ocean alone, facing it directly (abhimukha, pratimukha). "Tathā," in like manner, these of Yours — Bhīṣma and the rest — "narloka-vīrāḥ," the heroes (śūra) in the world of men — enter the mouths, which are "abhivijvalanti," blazing forth, shining.
BG_C11_V29: As moths enter a blazing fire to their destruction with quickened speed, so likewise do the worlds enter Your mouths to their destruction with quickened speed. (29)
BG_C11_V29::block-0: For what purpose, and in what manner, do they enter? He says —
BG_C11_V29::block-1: "Yathā" — just as — "pradīptam jvalanam," the blazing fire — "pataṅgāḥ," the winged creatures (birds, moths) — enter (viśanti) for destruction (nāśāya, vināśāya), being "samṛddha-vegāḥ" — those whose speed (vega), that is, motion (gati), is samṛddha, fully arisen, abundant — they are samṛddha-vegāḥ. "Tathaiva" — exactly so — for destruction the "lokāḥ," creatures (prāṇinaḥ), enter Your mouths likewise, with their speed fully arisen.
BG_C11_V30: Devouring the entire worlds from all sides with Your blazing mouths, You lick them up. Filling the entire universe with brilliance, Your fierce rays scorch, O Viṣṇu! (30)
BG_C11_V30::block-1: "Lelihyase" — You taste, You relish — "grasamānaḥ," causing them to enter within, swallowing — "samantāt," from every side — the "lokān samagrān," the worlds in their entirety — by means of "vadanaiḥ," mouths, "jvaladbhiḥ," blazing forth — "tejobhiḥ," with brilliances — "āpūrya," pervading thoroughly — "jagat samagram," the universe along with its foremost (sa-agra), that is, in its entirety. Furthermore, "bhāsaḥ," the radiances, "tava," Yours, "ugrāḥ," fierce, cruel — "pratapanti," they perform scorching, exert their heat — O Viṣṇu, that is, O One whose nature is to pervade (vyāpana-śīla).
BG_C11_V31: Tell me — who are You, of fierce form? Salutations to You, O best of gods; be gracious. I desire to know You, the Primordial One, in detail; for I do not comprehend Your activity. (31)
BG_C11_V31::block-0: Since His nature is thus fierce, therefore —
BG_C11_V31::block-1: "Ākhyāhi" — tell, declare — "me," to me — who is "bhavān," Your honour, of "ugra-rūpa," cruel form (krūrākāra)? Salutations be "te," to You, O "deva-vara," Foremost among the gods (devānāṃ pradhāna); "prasīda," bestow grace. "Vijñātum" — to know in a special, distinguished manner — "icchāmi," I desire — "bhavantam," Your honour — "ādyam," the Primordial — that which exists at the beginning (ādau bhava) is ādya. "Na hi" — for not — "prajānāmi," do I rightly comprehend — "tava," Your, that is, your own — "pravṛttim," activity, undertaking (ceṣṭā).
BG_C11_V32::block-0: "I am Time (Kāla), the destroyer of the worlds (loka-kṣaya-kṛt)" — He who effects the destruction (kṣaya) of the worlds is loka-kṣaya-kṛt — "pravṛddhaḥ," grown great, having attained increase. For what purpose I have grown great — hear that: "to gather (samāhartum), to dissolve (saṃhartum) the worlds, here, at this present time, am I engaged (pravṛttaḥ)." "Ṛte api" — even apart from, that is, even without "tvā," you — "na bhaviṣyanti," they shall not exist — Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa and the rest, all of them, with respect to whom there was apprehension on your part — "ye avasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu" — those who are stationed in the opposing armies; pratyanīkeṣu means among the anīkas (armies) ranged against (anīkam anīkaṃ prati) one another, that is, in the hostile (pratipakṣa-bhūta) anīkas — "yodhāḥ," the warriors (yoddhāraḥ).
BG_C11_V33: Therefore, you arise! Win renown! Having conquered the foes, enjoy the prosperous kingdom. By Me alone these have already been slain even before; be merely the instrument, O Savyasācin (ambidextrous archer Arjuna).
BG_C11_V33::block-1: Therefore you, arise! Win renown — that fame which runs, "Bhīṣma and others, the great car-warriors, unconquerable even by the gods, have been conquered by Arjuna." For such renown is attained only through abundant merits. Conquering the enemies — Duryodhana and the rest — enjoy the kingdom that is prosperous, free of rivals, free of thorns. By Me alone these have been slain — slain with certainty, separated from their life-breaths — already, beforehand. Be merely the instrument, O Savyasācin. Arjuna is called Savyasācin because he can discharge arrows with the savya, that is, the left hand also (as well as the right).
BG_C11_V34: Slay Droṇa, and Bhīṣma, and Jayadratha, and Karṇa, and the other warrior-heroes too — slain by Me. Do not be agitated. Fight! You shall conquer your rivals in battle.
BG_C11_V34::block-0: "Droṇa and the rest" — the Lord names by name precisely those warriors with regard to whom Arjuna had misgivings, saying, "slain by Me." Among them, the cause for misgiving in the case of Droṇa and Bhīṣma is well known. Droṇa is the preceptor of archery, endowed with celestial weapons, and especially Arjuna's own weighty teacher; Bhīṣma is one who dies at his own will, also endowed with celestial weapons, who entered single combat with Paraśurāma and was not defeated. Likewise Jayadratha, whose father practises austerity with the resolve, "He who shall cause my son's head to fall to the ground — his head too shall fall." Karṇa too is endowed with the unfailing Vāsava-given Śakti weapon; he is the son of Sūrya, born of an unwed maiden — and so is referred to by that very name (Karṇa). "Slain by Me" — these you slay, being merely the instrument. Do not be agitated — entertain no fear of them. Fight! You shall conquer Duryodhana and the rest — your rivals, your enemies — in battle, in the fray.
BG_C11_V35::block-0: Having heard this aforesaid speech of Keśava, the Diademed One (Kirīṭin, Arjuna), with folded palms, trembling, quivering, having made obeisance, again, once more, spoke — addressed — Kṛṣṇa with a faltering voice. When tears fill the eyes through grief at being seized by fear and through joy arising at being seized by affection, the throat is choked with phlegm; thence comes the indistinctness of speech, the feebleness of utterance — that is the faltering: along with that he spoke a faltering speech. This is a qualifier of the act of speaking. "Repeatedly fear-stricken," his mind again and again seized by fear, having bowed down — that is, having become humbly inclined — "he spoke": this is the connection across the intervening words.
BG_C11_V35::block-1: Sañjaya's speech at this juncture is freighted with intent. How? Thinking, "When the four unconquerable ones — Droṇa and the rest — are slain by Arjuna, Duryodhana, who is then without support, is as good as slain," Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having become hopeless about victory, will make peace; thence peace will come about for both sides — so [Sañjaya hoped]. Yet even that Dhṛtarāṣṭra did not heed, by the force of what was bound to be.
BG_C11_V36: Arjuna said: O Hṛṣīkeśa, fittingly does the world rejoice in Your praise, and rightly does it become attached to You; the rākṣasas, terrified, flee in all directions, and all the hosts of perfected ones bow down to You.
BG_C11_V36::block-0: "Fittingly" — that is, appropriately. What is appropriate? That, having heard Your praise — the proclamation of Your greatness, O Hṛṣīkeśa — the world rejoices, attains exultation: that is fitting, that is the meaning. Or, "fittingly" qualifies the object: the Bhagavān is the proper object of joy and the like, since He is the Lord, the Self of all, and the friend of all beings. Likewise it (the world) becomes attached, conceives affection — that too should be construed with reference to the [proper] object. Further, the rākṣasas, terrified — seized by fear — flee in the directions, run away; that too is fitting, with reference to the object. And all bow down — make obeisance — the assemblies of the Siddhas, the multitudes of the perfected ones such as Kapila and the rest; that too is fitting.
BG_C11_V37: And why should they not bow down to You, O Mahātman, the weightier than even Brahmā, since You are the primordial Author of even Brahmā? O Infinite One, O Lord of the gods, O Abode of the universe! You are the Imperishable, the Existent and the non-existent, and that which is beyond these.
BG_C11_V37::block-0: He shows the cause of the Bhagavān's being the proper object of joy and the like —
BG_C11_V37::block-1: And from what cause should they not bow down to You — make obeisance to You, O Mahātman, the weightier, the heavier in dignity? Since You are even the primordial Author — the cause — of Brahmā (Hiraṇyagarbha) himself, therefore [you are] the Ādikartṛ. How could these not bow down? Hence You are worthy, the proper object, of joy and the like and of obeisance — that is the meaning. O Infinite One, O Lord of the gods, O Abode of the universe! You are that supreme Imperishable (Akṣara) which is heard of in the Vedānta. What is that? "Sat-asat" — the Existent and the non-existent. Sat is what exists; asat is that wherein arises the cognition "it is not." These two — sat and asat — serve as the limiting adjuncts (upādhi) of which Akṣara, by means of which it is metaphorically spoken of as "sat-asat." In truth, however, that Akṣara is beyond both sat and asat — that Akṣara of which the knowers of the Veda speak. That [Akṣara] is You alone, none other — such is the import.
BG_C11_V38: You are the primordial Deity, the ancient Puruṣa; You are the supreme Resting-place of this universe. You are the Knower and the Knowable, and the supreme Abode. By You is the universe pervaded, O Form-without-end!
BG_C11_V38::block-1: You are the primordial Deity, since You are the creator of the world. The Puruṣa — so called from "lying in the city" (puri śayanāt). The Ancient (Purāṇa) — primeval — is You alone. You are the supreme — that is, the foremost — Resting-place (nidhāna) of this universe; that wherein, at the great dissolution and the like, the entire world is laid up. Further, You are the Knower (vettā) — the cogniser — of the entire class of objects-to-be-known. And whatever is to be known, fit to be cognised — that too You are. And [You are] the supreme Abode (paramaṁ dhāma) — the highest state, the Vaiṣṇava abode. By You is the universe — the entire whole — pervaded, suffused. O Form-without-end — there is no end of Your forms.
BG_C11_V39: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the Moon; You are Prajāpati and the Great-grandfather. Salutation, salutation be to You a thousand times; and again, yet again, salutation, salutation to You.
BG_C11_V39::block-1: You are Vāyu, and Yama, and Agni, and Varuṇa the lord of the waters, and Śaśāṅka — the moon. You are Prajāpati — Kaśyapa and the rest — and the Great-grandfather, the father even of the Grandfather (Pitāmaha): that is, the father even of Brahmā — such is the meaning. Salutation, salutation be to You a thousand times. And again, yet again, salutation, salutation to You. The repeated counting of the act of obeisance is expressed by the suffix "kṛtvasuc" (in sahasra-kṛtvas, a thousand times). By "again" and "yet again," through the excess of his faith and devotion, he shows his own non-satiation.
BG_C11_V40: Salutation to You from in front, and from behind! Salutation be to You from every side indeed, O All! Of infinite valour and immeasurable prowess, You pervade all; therefore You are All.
BG_C11_V40::block-1: Salutation to You from in front, in the eastern direction; then from behind, from the rear too, salutation be to You; from every side indeed — in all directions — to You who stand everywhere, O All! Anantavīrya-amitavikrama: His valour is infinite, His prowess is immeasurable. Vīrya is capacity, vikrama is exertion. Even one possessed of valour may, in the matter of slaying enemies and the like, not exert himself, or may exert himself feebly. You, however, are of infinite valour and of immeasurable prowess — hence anantavīrya-amitavikrama. Since You pervade — fully and with one Self compass — all, the entire world, therefore You are All; nothing exists apart from You — that is the import.
BG_C11_V41: Whatever was uttered by me presumptuously, deeming you merely a friend, addressing you as "O Kṛṣṇa, O Yādava, O comrade" — not knowing this greatness of yours — out of heedlessness or even from affection.
BG_C11_V41::block-0: Since I have offended through ignorance of your greatness, therefore —
BG_C11_V41::block-1: "Sakhā" — one of equal age; having so deemed, that is, having known you so through a mistaken cognition (viparīta-buddhi); "prasabham" — overpoweringly, forcibly, suppressing your true stature; whatever was uttered by me, namely, "O Kṛṣṇa, O Yādava, O comrade" — by one not knowing, that is, by the ignorant and deluded one. Not knowing what? He himself states it: "the greatness — the supreme dignity — that is yours, the Lord's, namely this Universal Form." The construction is to be taken with case-incongruity (vaiyadhikaraṇya) as "not knowing this greatness of yours." If, however, the reading "tavemam" obtains, then the agreement is in the same case (sāmānādhikaraṇya). "Out of heedlessness" — through distraction of mind; "or even out of affection" — praṇaya means the trustful familiarity born of love; through that cause too whatever I have spoken — [for all that I beg pardon].
BG_C11_V42: And whatever disrespect was shown to you in jest — in sport, on bed, on seat, at meals — whether alone or, O Acyuta, in the presence of others — for that I beg your pardon, you the immeasurable.
BG_C11_V42::block-0: And whatever — for the purpose of laughter, that is, for jesting — you have been disrespected, slighted; where? — in vihāra, śayyā, āsana and bhojana. Vihāra is the recreational stretching of the limbs, śayyā is the act of lying down, āsana is the seat or resting-place, bhojana is eating; in these — sport, bed, seat and meals — being alone, that is, in private, you have been slighted, dishonoured; or else, O Acyuta, even in the presence of others — the word "tat" here functions as an adverb qualifying the action — that is, openly, in public, you have been disrespected. All that aggregate of offences I beg you, the immeasurable, the one beyond every standard of measurement, to forgive.
BG_C11_V43: You are the Father of the world of the moving and the unmoving; you are its venerable one and the Guru, weightier than any other. There is none equal to you — how could there be another greater? — even in all the three worlds, O you of incomparable might.
BG_C11_V43::block-1: Father — that is, the begetter — of the world, of the entire host of living beings, of the moving and the unmoving, that is, of the mobile and the stationary. Not only are you the father of this universe, you are also pūjya — worthy of worship — because you are guru, the gurutara, weightier still. Why are you weightier? He explains: "There is none equal to you, none of like measure with you." For two Lords are not possible; were there many lords, the orderly transactions of the world would not stand. Even one merely equal to you is impossible; whence then could there be another greater — even in all the three worlds taken together? "Apratima-prabhāva" — pratimā is that by which something is measured; he whose prabhāva (might) has no pratimā is apratima-prabhāva; O you of incomparable might, that is, of unsurpassable might — such is the sense.
BG_C11_V44: Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I supplicate your favour, you the Lord, the praiseworthy. As a father with his son, as a friend with his friend, as a beloved with the beloved — so, O Lord, you ought to bear with me.
BG_C11_V44::block-1: "Therefore, having bowed down" — having offered namaskāra — "having prostrated" — that is, having held it well low down — "the body," I solicit the favour of you, the Lord, the ruler, the īḍya, the praiseworthy. And further: just as a father bears with the offence of his son, as a friend bears with everything in his friend's offences, or as a beloved bears with the offence of his beloved, even so, O God, you ought to bear — to endure, to forgive — such is the meaning.
BG_C11_V45: Having beheld what was never seen before, I am thrilled; yet my mind is shaken with fear. Show me, O God, that very form of yours [as before]; have grace, O Lord of gods, O abode of the worlds.
BG_C11_V45::block-0: "Adṛṣṭa-pūrvam" — never before seen by me or by any other — this Universal Form of yours; that I, having seen, am thrilled. Yet my mind is shaken with fear. Therefore show me — show me — that very form of yours, O God, that one which was friendly to me [before, as Vāsudeva]. Have grace, O Deveśa! "Jagan-nivāsa" — the abode of the worlds is jagan-nivāsa; O abode of the worlds!
BG_C11_V46: Crowned, mace-bearing, with discus in hand — I wish to behold you in that very same form, O thousand-armed one, O you of universal form. Be of that very form — the four-armed one [as before].
BG_C11_V46::block-0: "Kirīṭinaṁ" — bearing the diadem — and "gadinaṁ" — bearing the mace — and "cakra-hastam" — discus in hand — I wish, that is, I beseech you, to behold you, in that very same form, that is, as before. Since this is so, therefore in that very form — the form of the son of Vasudeva, the four-armed one — and not in this present sahasra-bāhu Universal Form, be, O Viśva-mūrte; that is, withdrawing the Universal Form, be in that very [familiar] form — such is the meaning.
BG_C11_V47::block-0: Perceiving Arjuna terrified, withdrawing the Universal Form, and reassuring him with kindly words, the Blessed Lord said —
BG_C11_V47::block-1: "By me, well-pleased" — prasāda is the disposition of grace toward you; possessed of that, well-pleased, by me, this supreme form, the Universal Form, has been shown to you, O Arjuna, "by my own yoga" — by the very might of my sovereign power. "Tejomayam" — abounding in radiance; "viśvam" — comprising the entire universe; "anantam" — without end; "ādyam" — that which was at the beginning, the primordial; that form of mine has not been seen before by any other than you.
BG_C11_V48: Not by the [study of] Vedas and sacrifices, not by gifts, not by ritual acts, not by fierce austerities, can I be seen in this form in the world of men by any other than you, O hero foremost of the Kurus.
BG_C11_V48::block-0: "You have indeed become fulfilled in your purpose by the very vision of my form" — thus he extols that vision —
BG_C11_V48::block-1: Not by the [study of the four] Vedas — that is, by the regular study of the four Vedas — and not by sacrificial study — although mastery of the Vedas alone already establishes mastery of the [knowledge of] sacrifices, the separate mention of yajña-adhyayana is by way of indicating the [whole] science of sacrifice; nor by gifts — such as the tulā-puruṣa and the like; nor by ritual acts — such as the agnihotra and the rest, prescribed by śruti and smṛti; nor even by ugra tapas — fierce, terrible austerities such as the cāndrāyaṇa and the like — am I, of such a form as has been displayed, that very Universal Form, capable of being beheld in this world of men by any other than you, O hero foremost of the Kurus.
BG_C11_V49: Let there be no terror in you, nor any bewilderment of mind, on having beheld this fearsome form of Mine such as this. With your fear gone and your heart at ease, behold once more this very form of Mine.
BG_C11_V49::block-0: Let there be no vyathā for you—that is, let there be no fear in you; nor any vimūḍha-bhāva, no bewildered condition of mind, on having beheld—on having perceived—this ghora rūpa, this fearsome form, ‘such as this’ (īdṛk), in the manner just shown to you, which is Mine.
